_comment: HAND-WRITTEN SAMPLE - this is documentation of the schema, not data.
The runtime loads markers/chapter1.json (no `.sample`), which tools/markers
produces from the cooked .umap cells. Every coordinate below is a real one
(the villager's from the extraction, the rest from the in-world recon dumps in
the task workspace), so the file is also
a usable smoke test: rename it to chapter1.json and these eight markers appear
at the places the recon found them.
Stable ids: a shrine uses the game-authored shrine id from BP_RebornFire_C's
CJK-named 'sitting-Buddha point ID' property; everything else uses
<owning level short name>/<cooked actor object name>, because that object name
is what FindAllOf hands back at runtime - it is the join key between this file
and the live actors.
Categories: shrine, chest, boss, elite, enemy, npc, note, door, ladder, lift,
fog_gate, hidden, other, plus the eleven pickup buckets - consumable, item,
harvest, ammo, armour, amulet, weapon, jade, spell, material, key. A pickup
that grants an item takes the bucket of its first item's E_ItemType; one with
no items takes its actor class' bucket (item / harvest / ammo) and its name
from the class default's own grant, where it has one. See
tools/markers/pickup_buckets.py. An `enemy` entry here is a SPAWN POINT,
not a live enemy: the runtime overwrites its position from the live pawn when
that pawn is streamed in, and enemies are never written to the collection
tracker. That is why the live sweep does not namespace enemy ids - the spawn
point and the live pawn must be one marker, not two.
Names: `name` is the game's own English name and `names` the same MMGame.locres
key in every other culture the game ships, only where it differs, keyed by the
locres folder name (de en es fr it ja ko pt ru zh zh-Hant; `zh` is Simplified
Chinese). A marker the game does not name carries neither and draws its
category's word in the player's language. One whose words are the mod's own
carries a `label` tag instead: `villager`, `workbench`, or `shrine` (read with
`fp` as 'Shrine <fire-point id>').
